## Active

### D-148 — The suite's Playwright run cannot resolve blong-marine's test dir

> _2026-09-12 · suite/blong-suite · active_

`blong-suite`'s Playwright run reports `Error: No tests found` because `resolveRealmTestDir` calls
`createRequire(import.meta.url)` from inside `blong-browser`, so `@feasibleone/blong-marine` cannot
be resolved from the suite. Marine's baselines therefore come from the marine app run instead. This
is pre-existing and unrelated to the baseline refresh.

### D-736 — A realm-profile deployment needs kubernetes resolution in release

> _2026-11-02 · suite/blong-suite · active_

A suite deployed with the `realm` profile runs one process per realm, and three things have to be
right before the browser can reach the API; `blong-suite` had none of them because it had only ever
run as a monolith test app.

`release: {resolution: {impl: 'kubernetes'}}` makes a dispatch another realm owns dial `<realm>`
instead of `127.0.0.1`, and it belongs in `release` and not `default` because a test run is not in a
cluster.

The portal's Ingress needs one path per namespace beside the portal's own: the portal's Service
reaches a single pod, and a pod answers only for the realms it carries. The generator now writes
`/rpc/<namespace>` → the Service named after that namespace, for every deployment whose name is one
of the namespaces it claims. That is what turned the browser's `POST /rpc/marine/coral/find` from
`Not Found` into an answer.

The portal's `realm` should be the process that carries the realms the menu draws on. `core` looked
right — it is the `both` realm, so it has a process of its own — but that process carries the
library realms alone; behind `marine` the same gateway also serves `marine.*`. They are separate
settings: the Ingress paths make split routing work, the portal's realm decides which pod is the
front door.

### D-794 — This deployment switches the suite's bundled mysql off

> _2026-11-08 · suite/blong-suite · active_

The suite's own declaration opts mysql in, which is right for a deployment that brings its database.
This cluster does not bring one: `db` in `blong-suite` is an ExternalName to
`mysql.blong-integration`, and the instance the declaration created in `blong-services` held no
table and no connection while the suite's pods ran against the shared instance for days. So this
deployment switches it off — `services: {mysql: false}` in the CR and in the local `.blong_k8src`,
which regenerates `local/declaration/blongdeployment.yaml` with the key set to false and drops
`local/namespaces/blong-services.yaml` and `local/suite/external-services/mysql.yaml` from the tree.

Removing `/spec/services` from the CR does not say that. With no key the operator planned the
service again: it recreated the `mysql` ExternalName in `blong-suite` within thirty-three seconds,
and the reconcile after that failed with
`5 step(s) failed, first: blong-services/persistent_volume_claim`, because the namespace it expected
had been deleted. The key has to be present and false — a switched-off service is still declared,
which is what the operator's cleanup sweep reads (@@D-651).

The suite keeps declaring the service rather than dropping it from `server.ts`: a tenant that wants
the bundled database still gets it, and a deployment that runs the shared one is the one that says
false. The slow statements that started this investigation are not caused by the second instance —
they are the shared server at its memory limit, tracked separately.

### D-739 — The portal realm still picks the bundle pod, not the RPC path

> _2026-11-02 · suite/blong-suite · active_

The portal's `realm` was load-bearing while the ingress fronted one Service: the pod behind it had
to answer every namespace the browser reached, which is why `core` answered `Not Found` for
`marine.*`. Since the tree writes `/rpc/<namespace>` per Service, that constraint is gone and `core`
would front the portal as well. `marine` is kept because it is the realm the suite is about and the
process the portal drives at steady state, and because the setting still decides the two things that
are left: which pod serves `/` and `/s/`, and where a namespace with no Service of its own lands —
the companions' namespaces. `blong` is no longer one of those: it rides the `core` process and has a
Service and a path of its own (`@@D-833`). Reconsider only if the portal should be served by the
smallest pod rather than the business one.
